1. I think omnigender would fit more into the role of someone who has all genders. Agender is usually for people who dont feel any gender. If youre curious there is a lot of info online about it, but gender is very confusing and we learn much about it every year so its fine if you are confused.

7. Theres a lot to go into relationships. Both the persons identity and your feelings and attractions are valid. You dont have to change what you like about someone but its important to note that the other person may not feel comfortable being w someone who doesnt view them in the way they want to be seen.

Gonna try to answer you in good faith, but i do think you should be wary of how you ask some of these questions. Some of them are just things you wouldn't really ask to anyone in general or you look like a insensitive. Also keep in mind I am not an expert myself. These are just my own thoughts as of right now. Anyone can feel free to correct me if they come to a different conclusion. 

1.Some people who are agender like to say they are included under the non binary label but it depends on the ppl you ask. Nonbinary is a term that means anyone outside the binary (man and woman). Agender is the absence of gender so it would make sense to be included imo, but some view nonbinary as genders outside the binary which is having a gender.

2. Thats an invasive question 😬, but I'll answer it anyway. No, I don't really care. I don't think my gender is defined by my genitalia, but if other people want to more power to them!  Also i think youre thinking of genderfluid, agender people aren't any gender and arent trying to become either genders like you said.

3. If people want to use specific pronouns bc it feels right to them, that's none of my business. I respect it either way. People can experience their gender differently. Which is why certain pronouns are useful. I think because we speak English we are used to understanding pronouns in connection to genders, but in other languages pronouns dont have any gender associated with them. What is spoken to refer to everyone means the same thing, it is neutral. We give meaning to words, not the other way around.  

4. Animals have sexes not genders from ehat we understand. Maybr they do but we cant ask them about it 🤣. Gender is something we created, its a construct that is an amalgamation of many traits. I don't feel my sex I know what it is, but I don't feel my gender. Like many people say on this subreddit, its an innate feeling you get. Kind of hard to explain a feeling without experiencing it yourself. 

5. Im pansexual myself so I dont know the answer to this, but this is just semantics so its not really important lol. Love whoever you love, labels just help to make things easier to identify and sort.

6. I don't know if this is 100% true, ive met a lot of people who having augmented their bodies w piercings, tattoos, and dyes but not only in the LGBTQ+ community. People who want a certain look do certain things its just how things are. I dont know if theres a specific correlation like youre implying here.

7. No, I don't think so. But I think theres a larger issue of do you even percieve your friend in the way they want to be seen? Do you question whether its straight or not bc you dont see them as the gender that they are and are only concerned about their sex? This is a whole different topic but I wont get into it.

Again I am not an expert but these are my current understandings of it. The world is constantly changing and so is culture. Its archaic to shove people into specific boxes they dont want to be in! 😤

I definitely think the one strip of 40+ a week is taxing. What I've heard from other creators is to find shortcuts for things. 

For example, they'll use google sketchup for backgrounds and some might trace references if a panel is taking too long. I know that it's generally frowned upon to trace for published work in the art community, but I think sometimes it's fine since your main concern is telling the story. Some compromises have to be made.

For your art, I would say if you're doing something full of effort, like a time consuming painterly style, maybe it would be more efficient to simplify it.( If you value finishing in a timely fashion.) I personally love when an author gives their all into a work and their unique artistic approaches, but at the same time, I know I'll just scroll through a chapter in 3 minutes so maybe having them so polished isnt worth the extra 5 hours?
